final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim to fit the existing record. That clarification is useful, but it does not satisfy the governing compliance predicate. The admissible evidence still shows an exposed below-target health-plan benefits support segment, no approved risk acceptance addressing that exposure, and no evidence of completed pre-launch disclosure. Under the stated policy, rollback capability, a 3% rollout, dashboards, and monitoring can mitigate only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable. Neither condition is met. The distinction matters: a caveated description of the weakness can make the packet more accurate, but accuracy of the writeup is not the same as compliance with the launch requirement. Because the unresolved issue is a substantive compliance condition rather than a mere overstatement problem, the proper final judgment remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The policy predicate for relying on rollout controls is not met because the affected use case is neither excluded nor covered by reviewed/approved risk acceptance.
The risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not mention the exposed health-plan benefits support segment.
The record does not show completed pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation for the named launch use case.
Public guidance on monitoring and model-card practice supports governance posture but does not satisfy the specific internal pre-launch policy requirement.
